text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden spike in serving-runtime pod restarts in us-west-2 (cluster: redwood-prod). Error observed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS / device address fault. Rolling error rate: 3.2% 5m, affected model: gpt-embed-v2, approx 1200 QPS impacted.

maria: I'm oncall, looking now. Any recent infra changes?

samir: noticed earlier — kernel/drivers didn't change. We had a small runtime rollout ~30m ago to push batching perf tweaks.

lee: throwing logs from one crashed pod: ```
E 23:41:12 runtime.cpp:453] cuda_kernel_launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
Backtrace: runtime::exec_stream +0x1a4
stack frame 0: device 0 pagewalk addr 0x7fffe000 misaligned
Container restarted by kubelet.
```

maria: ok, mark as HIGH. tagging runtime-team and ops-sre. Can we isolate by instance type / GPU model?

runtime-team: we see correlation with instances using driver 540.2 and a specific kernel ABI patch. Also a subset of requests with long context length. Not every pod fails — seems nondeterministic and more likely under concurrent KV cache attach.

ops-sre: starting mitigation: cordon node pool gpularge-1, scale down new rollout to 0 replicas, and start draining pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Will rotate pods one at a time.

maria: customer-impact: CS reported elevated error rates for 4 customers. customer-success, ping?

customer-success: confirmed. Two customers saw ~8% of generation calls fail briefly. No downstream data loss. They're asking for ETA on fix.

samir: quick mitigation attempt: disable persistent CUDA mappings in runtime config and reduce max_batch_size to 1 for the model route. Will patch configmap and rollout a canary. Command: ```kubectl set env deploy/serving-runtime RUNTIME_DISABLE_PERSISTENT_MAP=1 -n prod```

lee: also enabling CPU fallback for that route so heavy requests get served albeit slower: ```redwoodctl routes update --name gpt-embed-v2 --fallback cpu-small```

incident-bot: Handoff note: timeline created and incident channel locked to oncall participants. Create a short RCA ticket with initial hypothesis: device address misalignment due to kernel/driver interaction under KV cache attach.

maria: running nvml and dmesg collection on a pinned node and uploading to /tmp/triage/3060701234. Use `sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200` and `nvidia-smi -q -x`.

runtime-team: observed repeated page faults in kernel logs: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, reason: XnA memory access fault at 0x7f3b2c000
[ 1234.567901] kernel: __do_page_fault+0x... RIP: ...
```

samir: sounds like a kernel/device address race when the KV cache tries to reuse pages. Plan: revert the recent batching patch on the serving-runtime image for canary and add additional checks in the allocator to align device pointers.

maria: rolling back canary now. Patch applied: `image: registry.redwood/serving-runtime:2026-03-08-revert`. Rolling update in 5-min waves. Observability: error rate dropping?

ops-sre: after first wave, error rate down from 3.2% -> 0.9% in 10m. Pods on older image show stable. Continuing full rollout.

taylor: confirming mitigation: enabling node-level kernel panic on device faults is dangerous for multi-tenant — prefer process-level isolation and cordon instead. Good call to cordon gpularge-1.

customer-success: customers notified about transient failures and mitigations. One customer asked for logs; forwarded minimal sanitized dmesg and timeline.

runtime-team: we'll instrument allocation paths to avoid unaligned device pointers and add a runtime guard to reject mappings that would produce Xid 79. Adding tests for heavy-concurrency + KV cache on our CI cluster.

maria: handoff: I'll stay on till the rollout completes and error rate <0.2% for 30m. After that, hand to samir for overnight RCA and kernel-driver triage with vendor.

samir: acknowledged. I'll escalate to driver vendor with collected nvml/dmesg dumps and open kernel bug if needed.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: MITIGATION in place: rollback serving-runtime canary, cordon affected nodepool, CPU fallback enabled. Incident severity downgraded to SEV3.

lee: final notes: preserve the crashing pod's full core dump and set `kern.oops_on_fault=1` for an isolated repro node only. Saved to s3://redwood-incident-archives/3060701234/.

maria: last check at 3060702050: error rate steady at 0.15% 15m. Moving to monitoring state. Handoff complete to samir for deep dive. Thanks everyone. :bow:
